description: Trigger evals for branch-commit: it only names a branch and a short commit from a real diff (and can create that commit), while pr-package writes the full delivery write-up and the closure, state, review, and update commands work on memory, judgment, or messages.

should_trigger: what should I call this commit?
I have staged changes in scripts/lint-commands.sh and commands/task-init.md. Give me a branch name and a one-line commit message for them.
Slice 03 is finished and the working tree only touches src/billing/invoice.ts. Just write the commit message from the diff, I don't need anything longer than that.
My branch is still called wip-stuff and the diff against main only changes docs/FAQ.md. Suggest a better branch name and a commit subject.
Everything for this task is staged. Write the commit message, show me what is going in, and make the commit so the closure check finds one.

should_not_trigger.prompt: The scope is done and the diff against origin/main is stable. Write up the PR title, the description, and the reviewer notes for PR #212, and give me the git commands to push it.
I just committed the slice 02 changes. Update TASK_STATE.md so it shows what was done and I can pick this up again tomorrow.
Slice 03 is implemented and the tests pass. Is it ready to be closed, or is something still missing before I mark it done?
The diff is staged and ready. Before I commit, look it over for correctness bugs or anything risky I might have missed.
Write a short note for the team channel saying slice 02 is done and the change is committed on the task branch.
